statement: Wisp must validate, persist, retrieve, and report the durable state of a spec@1 artifact without relying on a coding harness or mutable sibling checkout.
why: The shared artifact path is the first portable handoff between Claude, Codex, and other harnesses; it must be reliable before Wisp adds derived cache, code intelligence, or MCP convenience.
done_when: A user can validate a spec@1 candidate against a pinned local schema and receive a machine-readable success or typed failure result.
A user can persist a valid spec@1 atomically at its deterministic docs/specs/<id>.json path and receive its raw-byte SHA-256 hash.
A user can retrieve a persisted spec@1 by ID and receive its canonical path, parsed artifact, content hash, and Git commit-state classification.
The commands work as a local CLI without Monokl, an MCP server, SQLite, vectors, or a running daemon.
The Rust workspace exposes build, test, lint, format, and CI-equivalent tasks through Moon and Just from its first implementation batch.
out_of_scope: plan@1 persistence and plan-to-spec freshness checks
automatic Git commits or remote pushes
MCP transport, TOON rendering, or Michi integration
SQLite, embeddings, document retrieval, or Monokl code evidence
